We have taken note of the media reports as well as a statement by the Global Fact-Checking Network (GFCN) that Google has indefinitely suspended the Association’s official account without the right to appeal or reinstatement. The GFCN was founded in 2024 and currently comprises 130 experts from 55 countries, including the US. There are also Russian specialists among its members and the renowned TASS news agency was among the founding members of the network. The Association is fairly new but has already earned a reputation for quality research.. It is a respectable fact-checking network that regularly publishes detailed refutations of disinformation and fake news. For example, in October, a group of GFCN experts published an in-depth analysis of the Bucha Hoax , a cynical falsification, designed and executed by the Kiev regime and its Western sponsors. Through facts, OSINT analysis, and having cross-referenced data, they have convincingly proven that most of the people mentioned at the memorial in Bucha are anything but “victims of Russian aggression”, some are in fact Azov members and combatants, some never existed. Could the act of censorship by Google be related to this high-profile research piece, which is an obvious soar spot for the Kiev regime and its sponsors as it debunks their lies? Or was the reason the GFCN’s independence and quality work be the reason? Even setting aside the fact that unilateral sanctions are illegitimate, GFCN, to the best of our knowledge, is not on any sanctions list. This is a clear act of arbitrary censorship with a poorly concealed political motive on the part of the tech giant. Against this backdrop, all assurances by its management regarding its commitment to the principles of freedom of access to information sound hollow. ❗️ We call on US tech corporations to uphold the principles of freedom of speech and equal access to critical information infrastructure — not just in words, but in deeds. If, however, this is indeed a mistake, it should be corrected without delay. This situation is yet another indication that without a full-fledged development of sovereign digital platforms and technologies, as well as fair competition of ideas, perspectives and thoughts, the transition to a truly multipolar world with equal opportunities for all its participants is hardly possible.
